title: Retention of the full visual opsin repertoire in Australia’s cryptozoic lizards
why: Sphenomorphus: the only work the harvest query "Sphenomorphus spectral sensitivity opsin" returned (1 hit), and the third hit of "Sphenomorphus vision", so its text probably names Sphenomorphus, perhaps as a comparison taxon. The stored abstract says that the five visual opsin genes were sequenced for 59 species of the Australian skinks Lerista and Ctenotus, so it may give the opsin genes, and so the likely cone classes, of a Sphenomorphus species (receptor_classes), and predicted pigment peaks (lambda_max_nm) if it models spectral tuning; an intact opsin gene predicts a pigment class, and only a spectral recording gives its peak. Main's sweep-79 logged one sentence from it for Lerista, and harvest-36 put it on the wanted list for Eutropis, so its text has not been read for Sphenomorphus. The web pair "Sphenomorphus spectral sensitivity" and "forest skink spectral sensitivity" returned no skink pigment study of this genus. Not opened.

title: Etude comparative de la morphologie de l'oeil chez quatre espèces de lézards tropicaux (Scincidae) occupant différentes niches écologiques
why: Sphenomorphus: a 2024 poster from the Université de Mons comparing eye morphology in four tropical skink species that occupy different ecological niches. The harvest stores no abstract ("editorial reviewed"), so the four species are not visible. It came back in the Scincidae family review of the harvest and for the web searches "forest skink visual acuity", "forest skink visual field" and "forest skink pupil shape", with its abstract PDF (bitstream 51244/2). A Sphenomorphus species could be among the four, since the genus is tropical, and eye morphology can give eye and lens dimensions that bear on acuity_cpd, whether the retina has a fovea (fovea) and a pupil shape (pupil_shape). Main's harvest-37 put the same poster on the wanted list for Trachylepis. The author is the name the file name shows. Not opened.

title: Sphenomorphus tamchucensis sp. nov. (Squamata, Scincidae), a new skink from Vietnam
why: Sphenomorphus: the first result of the web search "Sphenomorphus pupil shape" (its PubMed Central copy, PMC12820565), and a hit of the harvest queries "Sphenomorphus eye" and "Sphenomorphus visual field". It describes a new forest skink from Vietnam, and descriptions of skinks give the external characters of the head and eye, so its text may state the shape of the pupil (pupil_shape), which main accepts from species descriptions (sweep-56#5). The stored abstract lists size and scalation characters and names no pupil. The same search returned the ZooKeys description of S. puhoatensis (10.3897/zookeys.1279.188050, also in the harvest), which may state it as well. Not opened.
